subject: ventures/iban-list-check
professional: a payments operations / treasury specialist who validates supplier and payroll IBAN lists before a SEPA batch. What they check first: ISO 13616 mod-97 including the 02-98 check-digit range, the per-country length and BBAN structure from the current SWIFT IBAN Registry, national check digits where the country defines them, and that a clean exit really means every row in the payee column was checked

evidence.correctness: Ran node ventures/iban-list-check/cli.mjs check /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-oss-monorepo/096f4309-df66-5732-9d71-6aa6a7962eea/scratchpad/iban/list.csv (30 rows) and list2.csv, two.csv, sepa.csv, with expectations from an independent Python mod-97 (/tmp/claude-0/-home-user-oss-monorepo/096f4309-df66-5732-9d71-6aa6a7962eea/scratchpad/iban/ref.py, int(c,36) letter mapping and Python big ints) and the SWIFT IBAN Registry release 101 as tabulated by python-stdnum (stdnum/iban.dat, fetched from GitHub). Right: all 14 registry example IBANs for countries the tool knows pass (GB, DE, FR, NL, BE, ES, IT, PT, NO, PL, CH, AT, LC, SC); 3 single-character / transposition errors are errors and the transposition gets the correct swap among 2 candidates; a 21-char DE is 'wrong length (1 missing)'; lower case, spaces, hyphens and an 'IBAN:' label are cleaned and then caught as duplicates; BE and ES IBANs whose account was mistyped and ISO digits recomputed raise the national-check warning, as do FR, IT, PT, NO and PL single-digit mutants (5 of 5; the PL account-part mutant correctly does not, since the PL check covers only the sort code). All 77 country lengths in COUNTRIES match registry v101 exactly. Wrong: (1) DE01370400440000000042, DE00370400440000000060 and DE99370400440000000024 are reported valid; ISO 13616 check digits are 02-98, and these are the aliases of 98, 97 and 02 that a mod-97-only test lets through, so a bank's validator rejects what the tool passed; (2) RU, LY, OM and MN registry examples are errors 'Not a valid IBAN: unknown country'; 12 registry countries are missing (BI, DJ, FK, HN, LY, MN, NI, OM, RU, SD, SO, YE); (3) --column payee_iban is silently ignored and the tool checks the first IBAN-named column instead, exit 0 with a bad payee IBAN.
evidence.completeness: Claimed features checked: mod-97 with swap suggestion (works); length per country (works for the 77 it lists); unknown countries (works, but over-fires on 12 registry countries); clean-up of spaces, lower case, labels (works); duplicates and blanks (works); per-line numbers (works); SEPA-only flag (works, conservative list); national check digits for BE ES FR IT PT NO PL (works on 7 of 7); CLI check/fix/--json/--strict/directory walk (works). Broken: the page's 'Write IBANs in groups of four' checkbox does nothing: index.html:160 passes {excelSafe} while repair() reads options.groups (node: repair(t,{excelSafe:true}) returns unbroken text, repair(t,{groups:true}) returns groups); the served page at https://marisstella.app/iban-list-check/ carries the same excelSafe line. The CLI --column <name> documented in help, README:23 and cli.mjs:7 does not select by name. No stubs or TODOs.
evidence.verification: cd ventures/iban-list-check && node --test '*.test.mjs': 40 tests, 40 pass, 0.19 s. Seeded 9 mutations with platform/ci/quality_mutate.py (one more, removing the equal-character skip in findTransposition, was equivalent and is not counted). Only 1 caught (duplicate detection). Survived: accepting mod97 remainder 0 (calc.mjs:36), treating too-long IBANs as fine at the length gate (calc.mjs:123), changing the LC length 32->31 (calc.mjs:10), dropping the ES 10->1 rule (calc.mjs:44), the NO remainder-1 rule (calc.mjs:65), the BE 0->97 rule (calc.mjs:49), the PL %10 wrap (calc.mjs:70), and fixing the page's excelSafe/groups mismatch (index.html:160) changes no test outcome. The national-check tests only use one valid example and one forgery per country, so every edge branch is untested; there is no test that --column accepts a header name.
evidence.craft: Read calc.mjs (242 lines), cli.mjs (118), index.html script, page.test.mjs, calc.test.mjs. Small, dependency-free, pure functions, BigInt where 32-bit would overflow, line numbers kept through quoted newlines. Defects: parseTable computes the delimiter ranking twice in one expression (calc.mjs:86-87); pickColumn coerces the override with Number() and falls through silently for a name (calc.mjs:147-148) instead of matching the header or failing; the page and the engine disagree on the option name (excelSafe vs groups); checkOk tests remainder only, not the 02-98 range.
evidence.claims: Backed: 'file is never uploaded' (page.test.mjs asserts no fetch/XHR/beacon and local-only imports); disclaimer and independence notes on README, page and served page; 'country list read from memory' stated on the page; lengths in the FAQ (DE 22, GB 22, FR 27, NL 18, ES 24, IT 27, BE 16, CH 21) match registry v101. Not backed: 'Not checked: national check digits for countries other than BE, ES, FR and IT' (index.html:114, :131 and the JSON-LD FAQ at :12) is stale: PT, NO and PL are also checked (index.html:110 says so); '--column <name|n>' (cli.mjs:23, README:23) does not work for names; the 'groups of four' option on the page does nothing; 'wrong check digits' caught, while 00/01/99 pass; llms.txt boilerplate 'Results are estimates from the numbers typed in' does not describe a validator. Served llms.txt has marisstella.app URLs (rewritten at deploy, not a defect).
evidence.fitness: Walked the job: a supplier CSV for a SEPA batch, checked with the CLI and with --sepa-only. Every EU/EEA/CH/GB country is in the table with the registry length and, for 18 of them, the BBAN shape; mod-97 is right; the national checks for BE, ES, FR, IT, PT, NO and PL go beyond most free validators; findings carry line numbers and the fix file keeps other columns. A treasury clerk could use it as a pre-flight with the stated limits. Gaps hit in the first hour: a file with payer and payee IBAN columns needs the column number, not the name, or the payee column is silently skipped; the print-format checkbox on the page is dead; non-SEPA payees in 12 registry countries are flagged invalid; GI (in SEPA) is flagged as outside the core list.
evidence.domain: Against ISO 13616-1 and the SWIFT IBAN Registry v101: the mod-97 algorithm and the 77 lengths are right; the BBAN shapes it states (DE, AT, BE, ES, DK, FI, NO, PL, PT, SE, CZ, SK, HR, SI, GB, NL, IE, LU) agree with the registry's BBAN formats. Departures: ISO 13616 check digits must be in 02-98 and the tool accepts 00, 01 and 99; the registry has 89 countries and the tool 77 (missing ones added 2021-2024: BI, DJ, FK, HN, LY, MN, NI, OM, RU, SD, SO, YE); the SEPA list leaves out Gibraltar (in the EPC geographic scope for years) and the 2025 joiners, which it warns on rather than errors, the conservative choice. National algorithms (BE mod 97 with 0->97, ES weights 1,2,4,8,5,10,9,7,3,6 with 10->1, FR RIB key 89/15/3 with letter folding, IT CIN odd/even tables, PT 98-mod97, NO mod 11, PL 3,9,7,1 sort-code check) match the published national rules as I know them and passed on the registry examples and 7 forgeries.

verdict: A tidy, private IBAN pre-flight whose mod-97 arithmetic, 77 country lengths and seven national check-digit algorithms are right on every registry example and forgery I ran. It does not meet the bar: it passes IBANs with check digits 00/01/99 that ISO 13616 forbids, rejects valid IBANs from 12 registry countries as invalid, silently ignores the documented --column <name> (a payee column can go unchecked with exit 0), ships a dead 'groups of four' checkbox, and its tests catch 1 of 9 seeded bugs. Fitness for a SEPA-only batch is close to professional; verification is the weakest dimension.
